title: FCA stops HTX's crypto promotions
summary: The FCA has secured High Court undertakings to ensure that HTX (formerly Huobi), a global crypto exchange, will not knowingly promote cryptoasset services unlawfully to UK consumers. The FCA took legal action against HTX in October 2025 for breaking UK financial promotion rules. HTX had failed repeatedly to engage with the FCA. Following the commencement of proceedings, HTX took steps to exit the UK. The FCA and Huobi Global S.A. have now reached a settlement in the case. HTX is no longer active in the UK. Consumers can no longer make deposits, and new UK users cannot sign up to the platform. HTX will not target, solicit or actively seek to engage UK consumers.UK users of HTX should read the information published on HTX's website about the availability of its services in the UK and the arrangements for withdrawing any residual assets.Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said: 'Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law. Our action means HTX is leaving the UK and can no longer target UK consumers. The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.'

title: 2026-10-29 - Petra Tschudin / Thomas Moser: Liquidity against collateral: the SNB's approach
summary: In order to perform its statutory tasks, the SNB provides the financial system with central bank liquidity against sufficient collateral. The SNB's collateral policy protects its balance sheet and ensures that liquidity is provided in an effective, efficient and transparent manner. The SNB GC Basket plays a key role in the implementation of monetary policy and in supporting payments. It combines high quality requirements with a broad, international focus, and has also become established as the collateral standard in the Swiss interbank repo market. This common standard and the integrated market infrastructure facilitate the mobilisation of collateral, thereby supporting the effective implementation of monetary policy and the smooth functioning of payments. The SNB reviews its collateral policy on an ongoing basis and adjusts it as necessary to take account of changed market conditions and technological developments.

title: ES - 2026-10-29 - Damien Klossner, Igor Mlikota and Sabrina Stadelmann: What collateral is used in the Swiss interbank repo market?
summary: Collateral is a key component of repurchase agreement transactions. We document collateral usage in the Swiss interbank repo market using an extensive transaction-level dataset. We find that a substantial share of securities eligible for the SNB General Collateral Basket is actively used, particularly securities denominated in Swiss francs. Collateral usage is concentrated in a small number of issuers and highly rated securities denominated in Swiss francs. At the same time, it displays a broad and balanced maturity profile, and cross-currency repos account for a meaningful share of trading volume.
